I don't believe in inalienable rights. All rights can be (and historically have been) taken away from groups or individuals under the right circumstances. If something cannot be taken away, it isn't a right, it's an inherent quality or ability. The entire idea of "rights" is that we have decided, as a species, that there are certain things we ideally want to guarantee to all people. This does not mean those rights cannot ever be taken away, but that any action or circumstance that would interfere with those rights or attempt to take them away intentionally should be highly suspect and usually prevented.

Rights and their rules change throughout history. It is based on culture. If it is commonly considered morally wrong to use violence to stop someone from doing something, that person has a right to do it. In turn government laws loosely reflect the current cultural climate of when force is acceptable to interfere with someone's actions. Legally rights start when the laws say they do. Culturally rights start when it is commonly believed they do. Every right is different.
